# Delivery routing ruling (e2e synthetic)

Tanya (team owner) ruled on where reaction delivery belongs:

> we route every reaction through one bundle per run per person, not one
> message per skill — a person should get one thing to read, not four

Tina pushed back on the batching window and Tanya held: the bundle closes when
the run closes, and a skill that misses the close waits for the next run rather
than sending on its own. The alternative considered and rejected was per-skill
delivery with client-side collapsing, which moves the ordering problem onto the
reader.

payload.rationale: I called perspective once and expanded the Thematic and Documents doors. The graph is almost entirely product-positioning material (anti-Slack narrative, real-time chat anti-pattern, context preservation next sprint), and the only other area is the ungrouped anti-Slack narrative. I expanded the anti-Slack narrative and the two positions whose frames the bundling-versus-per-message decision could brush: the anti-real-time-chat stance and the decision-artifact framing. I did not expand the Pricing, Target Market, Webhook, or Zephyr positions, nor the Decisions Evaporate and Decision Capture narratives, because nothing in the ruling touches pricing, market, architecture, or the decision-capture thesis directly. The document is an internal delivery-mechanics ruling, so the surfaced context is a loose frame, not a direct answer to any existing position.

positions.name: ReactionDeliveryRouting
positions.frame: how should reaction delivery be bundled and windowed across skills per run?
positions.why: Establishes the routing policy for reactions (one bundle per run per person rather than per-skill messages), defines the batching window lifecycle against pushback, and rules out client-side collapsing to protect the reader from ordering overhead.

placements.why: Tanya's ruling that reactions must be routed through one bundled delivery per run per person—preventing per-skill notification floods and rejecting client-side collapsing—directly enforces the anti-Slack thesis of structured async decision communication over real-time chat noise.

connections.why: Defines the core architectural routing policy of bundling reactions per run per person and closing the window at run completion.
